Carbon Robotics reduces workforce, citing economic conditions

The LaserWeeder maker confirms cuts across departments in the US and internationally without disclosing their size.

GeekWire ↗20 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

The company confirms cuts

GeekWire reported on the evening of October 19 in Seattle that Carbon Robotics confirmed workforce reductions across multiple departments in the US and internationally. Marketing vice president Brett Goodwin attributed the move to aligning costs with economic conditions and said the company employs 275 people worldwide. The number of layoffs was not disclosed.

The agricultural technology involved

Its LaserWeeder G2 is pulled behind a tractor and uses AI to detect and map plants before targeting weeds with lasers. Founded in 2018, Carbon Robotics has raised about $177 million. A $20 million financing and autonomous-tractor-kit announcement occurred in 2025, rather than being new product developments in this update.

Do not infer product changes without evidence

The report documents a cost adjustment at an agricultural robotics supplier. It does not state that a product line is closing or customer service is stopping, so delivery consequences cannot yet be concluded. Technology capabilities, staffing and financial plans should be assessed separately because the available disclosures differ.
